# Software Design Document (SDD)

<!-- Generated by `omni docs build` (REQ-060) for Arbiter. Do not edit; regenerate. -->

What each part of Arbiter is for: 85 module(s) in 4 package(s). Each package gets one line in the table below, then one line per module: its purpose (from the module docstring), the public types it defines, how many project modules import it, and the design reason when the docstring gives one.

Where the rest lives: per-module import lists in the [Module Reference](modules.md), class relationships in the [Class Diagram](class-diagram.md), which files and tests belong to each requirement in the [Requirements Traceability Matrix](requirements-traceability.md). `omni docs build --detail full` writes every public signature, class and method here instead.

Embedded OmniEngineering tooling is not described here: `make_ai.py`, `omni_docs.py`, `omni_graph.py`, `omni_mcp.py`.

## Package src/arbiter

- [__init__.py](../../src/arbiter/__init__.py): Arbiter — a polyglot repository and system evaluator.
- [ab.py](../../src/arbiter/ab.py): A/B harness. Defines `Arm`, `ArmResult`, `Match`, `GroundTruthResult` (+1 more). 9 public functions.
- [adapters.py](../../src/arbiter/adapters.py): Declarative adapters for external analyzers. Defines `AdapterOutputError`, `AnalyzerErrors`, `Adapter`. 8 public functions. Why: An adapter is a TOML manifest: how to invoke a tool, how to parse it, and how to map its output onto Finding. No Python is written per tool, which is what keeps the long tail of languages tractable.
- [aiapp.py](../../src/arbiter/aiapp.py): App-level defects found in AI-written services (ARB-083). 2 public functions. Imported by 1 module. Why: The language packs see one file and one function. (more: [src/arbiter/aiapp.py](../../src/arbiter/aiapp.py) docstring)
- [api.py](../../src/arbiter/api.py): The hosted front door: Arbiter as something a customer calls, not installs. Defines `RateLimited`, `RateLimiter`, `FileRateLimiter`, `AuditLog`. 17 public functions. Why: This is the second surface over `service.py`, alongside `mcp.py`. It decides nothing about containment -- workspaces, archive safety, path limits and profile limits all live in the service layer, so they are written once.
- [assurance.py](../../src/arbiter/assurance.py): Is the checking switched on? 2 public functions. Imported by 1 module. Why: Every scanner on the market will hand you the same green tick for both. They have to: they honour the suppression comments, they honour the ignore files, and a test that asserts nothing still passes. (more: [src/arbiter/assurance.py](../../src/arbiter/assurance.py) docstring)
- [ast.py](../../src/arbiter/ast.py): Tree-sitter layer. Defines `FunctionInfo`. 11 public functions. Why: This is what makes "polyglot" real rather than aspirational: function boundaries, nesting depth and branch complexity are read from a parse tree instead of guessed from indentation, and the same code works for every grammar in the pack.
- [authored.py](../../src/arbiter/authored.py): Defects characteristic of machine-authored code. 5 public functions. Imported by 1 module. Why: A large and growing share of new code is drafted by a language model, and model-drafted code fails in ways human-drafted code mostly does not. (more: [src/arbiter/authored.py](../../src/arbiter/authored.py) docstring)
- [bundle.py](../../src/arbiter/bundle.py): The air-gapped bundle: Arbiter as a directory that installs with no network. Defines `BundleError`, `VerifyResult`. 5 public functions. Why: A bundle is a directory holding the wheel of Arbiter itself, the wheels of its runtime dependencies, the calibration knowledge file when the checkout carries one, two install scripts and a manifest with a SHA-256 per file. (more: [src/arbiter/bundle.py](../../src/arbiter/bundle.py) docstring)
- [cache.py](../../src/arbiter/cache.py): Persistent per-file result cache for file-local probes. Defines `ResultCache`. 10 public functions. Why: Reading was never the bottleneck -- the in-process read cache in probes.py proved that -- but analysis is, and every scan paid for all of it again. (more: [src/arbiter/cache.py](../../src/arbiter/cache.py) docstring)
- [claims.py](../../src/arbiter/claims.py): Claim integrity. Defines `Claim`, `Violation`. 7 public functions. Why: Arbiter's central promise is that it never asserts something it did not verify. Stated in prose that is a design principle; stated here it is a machine-checkable invariant with a test suite behind it.
- [cli.py](../../src/arbiter/cli.py): Command line interface. 21 public functions.
- [client.py](../../src/arbiter/client.py): The client half: reach a hosted Arbiter instead of installing one. Defines `ClientError`. 8 public functions. Why: Every other surface in this package runs the scanner where the repository is. This one does not run it at all. (more: [src/arbiter/client.py](../../src/arbiter/client.py) docstring)
- [concurrency.py](../../src/arbiter/concurrency.py): Shared state touched by concurrent workers without a lock (ARB-053, ARB-054). 2 public functions. Imported by 1 module. Why: The most common defect in model-drafted worker code is not a wrong algorithm, it is a race: a queue that checks it has an item and then takes it, a counter bumped from several threads. (more: [src/arbiter/concurrency.py](../../src/arbiter/concurrency.py) docstring)
- [context.py](../../src/arbiter/context.py): What a model is shown about one finding: a bounded, deterministic excerpt (ARB-067). Defines `Limits`, `RepoView`, `Definition`, `Context`. 12 public functions. Why: Used by the model labellers (`tools/label_models.py`, through `tools/ground_truth/gt_common.excerpt`) and by the verification pass (`verify.py`), so the two see the same code for the same finding.
- [contract.py](../../src/arbiter/contract.py): Contracts declared in one artifact and implemented in another. 3 public functions. Imported by 1 module. Why: Each half is valid on its own terms. The spec parses, the routes compile, the migrations apply. No linter compares them, because each tool sees one side. (more: [src/arbiter/contract.py](../../src/arbiter/contract.py) docstring)
- [controls.py](../../src/arbiter/controls.py): Control frameworks, and an honest account of what was actually assessed. Defines `Control`, `Framework`. 8 public functions. Why: An accreditation package built on that is worse than no package, because a reader cannot tell which controls carry evidence.
- [core.py](../../src/arbiter/core.py): Core data model for Arbiter. Defines `Location`, `Finding`, `ProbeOutcome`, `RepoInfo` (+3 more). 4 public functions. Why: Everything in the pipeline speaks Finding. Probes produce them, adapters normalize into them, reporters render them, and the A/B harness matches on their fingerprints.
- [cwe.py](../../src/arbiter/cwe.py): CWE classification for every finding, native or external. 3 public functions. Why: Native rules declare their CWE here (or, for a language pack rule, in the pack itself). External analyzers report it in their own output, read through the adapter manifest's `cwe` / `cwe_const` map keys and normalised by `normalise`. (more: [src/arbiter/cwe.py](../../src/arbiter/cwe.py) docstring)
- [dataflow.py](../../src/arbiter/dataflow.py): Intraprocedural, one-hop data flow for the language packs (Milestone 3). Defines `Budget`, `AV`, `Spec`, `Interp`. 11 public functions. Why: Rule queries match one statement's shape. Code a model writes moves the same defect around: the SQL built into a variable on the line before, the request value passed through a small helper, the `"sh"` literal hoisted into a constant. (more: [src/arbiter/dataflow.py](../../src/arbiter/dataflow.py) docstring)
- [diff.py](../../src/arbiter/diff.py): Report-to-report comparison. Defines `ReportDiff`. 3 public functions. Why: The number that changes behavior is the delta, not the absolute score. This is what the CI gate reads when `fail_on.new` is set and what the pull-request comment leads with.
- [ecosystems.py](../../src/arbiter/ecosystems.py): Imports and manifests for Go, Java and Ruby (Python and JS live in authored.py). 17 public functions. Why: Each ecosystem answers three questions for the undeclared-import check: which names does a file import, which does the repository declare, and which are standard library or the repository's own code. (more: [src/arbiter/ecosystems.py](../../src/arbiter/ecosystems.py) docstring)
- [engine.py](../../src/arbiter/engine.py): The scan pipeline: acquire → inventory → plan → execute → normalize → correlate → score → report. 7 public functions. Why: Stages are separate so each is testable on its own and so a probe failure is contained: one probe erroring degrades to 'not assessed' for that probe and never fails the run.
- [globs.py](../../src/arbiter/globs.py): Globstar path matching for house rules (ARB-147). 2 public functions. Why: A pattern with no `/` is matched against the whole path too, so `*.py` means the root's `.py` files -- `**/*.py` is "any depth", as it is everywhere else.
- [graph.py](../../src/arbiter/graph.py): Provider-neutral resource graph. Defines `Resource`. 12 public functions. Why: Terraform HCL, CloudFormation / CDK-synthesized templates and Kubernetes manifests all normalize into one Resource shape, so a policy is written once against a normalized `kind` and fires on every provider.
- [history.py](../../src/arbiter/history.py): Run history and the trend dashboard. 4 public functions. Why: Every report is a complete record of one run. What it cannot show is the direction: whether coverage has been sliding for a month, whether the high count that failed today's gate was two yesterday or twenty. (more: [src/arbiter/history.py](../../src/arbiter/history.py) docstring)
- [incremental.py](../../src/arbiter/incremental.py): Scanning only what changed, and saying so. 11 public functions. Why: A full scan of Traefik — 452,000 lines — takes about two minutes. That is fine once a night and useless on every pull request, where the answer is wanted before the author has switched windows. The obvious fix is to make the scan faster. (more: [src/arbiter/incremental.py](../../src/arbiter/incremental.py) docstring)
- [inventory.py](../../src/arbiter/inventory.py): Acquire targets and classify what is in them. Defines `FileInfo`, `Inventory`, `Acquired`. 6 public functions. Imported by 1 module. Why: Acquire turns a target (local path, git URL, or a multi-repo system manifest) into read-only workspaces. (more: [src/arbiter/inventory.py](../../src/arbiter/inventory.py) docstring)
- [judgement.py](../../src/arbiter/judgement.py): The model-backed judgement pass. Defines `Unavailable`, `Provider`, `AnthropicProvider`. 4 public functions. Imported by 1 module. Why: Everything else in Arbiter answers questions with a definite shape: is this property set, does this value match this pattern, does this address appear in two repositories with different values. (more: [src/arbiter/judgement.py](../../src/arbiter/judgement.py) docstring)
- [lang_rules.py](../../src/arbiter/lang_rules.py): Shipped per-language rule packs: structural checks for every IDE language. Defines `PackError`. 10 public functions. Why: Most native checks were written for Python first. (more: [src/arbiter/lang_rules.py](../../src/arbiter/lang_rules.py) docstring)
- [learn.py](../../src/arbiter/learn.py): Learning, without breaking reproducibility. Defines `RuleStats`, `Verdict`, `Knowledge`. 11 public functions. Why: An evaluator that adapts and an evaluator that is reproducible are in direct tension: if a scan's behaviour depends on history, the same commit can pass on Monday and fail on Tuesday, and a baseline, a CI gate and an accreditation artefact all stop meaning anything.
- [ledger.py](../../src/arbiter/ledger.py): Draft OmniEngineering failure-ledger entries from true-positive verdicts. 2 public functions. Why: Arbiter's adjudication ledger (`.arbiter/knowledge.json`) and the OmniEngineering failure ledger (`.ai/failures/failure-ledger.json`) both record what was wrong and why, and until now in parallel: a reviewer marked a finding real, fixed it, and then described the same defect a second time for the workspace. (more: [src/arbiter/ledger.py](../../src/arbiter/ledger.py) docstring)
- [mcp.py](../../src/arbiter/mcp.py): Model Context Protocol surface: Arbiter as tools an agent can call. 6 public functions. Why: This is one of two front doors over `service.py`, which holds the containment rules. The other is the hosted API. (more: [src/arbiter/mcp.py](../../src/arbiter/mcp.py) docstring)
- [planted.py](../../src/arbiter/planted.py): The planted corpus: known defects, each beside a correct twin. Defines `Expected`, `Score`. 3 public functions. Why: Markers live on the defect line itself, so they cannot drift away from it the way a separate list of line numbers would.
- [policy.py](../../src/arbiter/policy.py): Configuration, profiles, suppressions, scoring and the gate. 15 public functions. Why: Scoring exists to drive behavior, not to be precise. Two properties matter more than the formula: findings are normalized by codebase size, and the grade is withheld when too little of the rubric could actually be evaluated.
- [precision.py](../../src/arbiter/precision.py): Precision tiers: which findings may block a gate, on what evidence. Defines `UnknownPopulation`. 20 public functions. Why: The verdict is read from `finding.verification` (the verify pass) when it is there, through `getattr`, so this module works with or without that pass.
- [probes.py](../../src/arbiter/probes.py): Native probes. Defines `ProbeContext`, `Probe`. 13 public functions. Imported by 2 modules. Why: Every probe here runs with nothing installed but Python. (more: [src/arbiter/probes.py](../../src/arbiter/probes.py) docstring)
- [report.py](../../src/arbiter/report.py): Reporters. 19 public functions.
- [review.py](../../src/arbiter/review.py): Batch adjudication: making the one irreplaceable input cheap enough to give. 6 public functions. Why: Calibration reads one ledger and one only: findings a person looked at and judged right or wrong. Not the injection trials, which measure whether a rule works mechanically against faults the tool itself generated. (more: [src/arbiter/review.py](../../src/arbiter/review.py) docstring)
- [review_ui.py](../../src/arbiter/review_ui.py): Two front ends for adjudication, over one sampler and one ledger. 3 public functions. Why: Calibration reads exactly one ledger: findings a person looked at and judged right or wrong. Not the injection trials, which measure whether a rule works mechanically against faults the tool generated for itself. (more: [src/arbiter/review_ui.py](../../src/arbiter/review_ui.py) docstring)
- [rule_meta.py](../../src/arbiter/rule_meta.py): Rule metadata that is not detection logic: requirements, tier, precision ref. Defines `RuleMetaError`. 7 public functions.
- [scope_notes.py](../../src/arbiter/scope_notes.py): Scope notes: read a scanned repo's own docs so a finding can carry a pointer to a control the repo's authors say already covers it. Defines `ScopeNote`. 2 public functions. Why: A heading matching SCOPE_HEADING (case-insensitive: "out of scope", "known limitations", "external controls", "handled elsewhere", "compensating controls") opens a scope-note section. (more: [src/arbiter/scope_notes.py](../../src/arbiter/scope_notes.py) docstring)
- [service.py](../../src/arbiter/service.py): One service layer, two front doors. Defines `ServiceError`, `Workspace`. 7 public functions. Why: Arbiter is growing a second caller. The MCP surface lets an agent run a scan on a machine where Arbiter is already installed; the hosted API lets a caller run one where it is not. Those differ only in transport. (more: [src/arbiter/service.py](../../src/arbiter/service.py) docstring)
- [supply.py](../../src/arbiter/supply.py): Supply-chain pinning: is what gets built what was reviewed? 33 public functions. Why: Each check here answers one mechanical question about one file -- is this reference to third-party code immutable? -- and is called from `probes.probe_supply_chain`. (more: [src/arbiter/supply.py](../../src/arbiter/supply.py) docstring)
- [supply_deps.py](../../src/arbiter/supply_deps.py): Package-manifest pinning: Python, npm, Maven/Gradle, RubyGems, Terraform. 16 public functions. Why: The ecosystem half of src/arbiter/supply.py (which holds the shared helpers, the CI and container checks, and the dispatch). What counts as pinned in each ecosystem is listed in that module's docstring. (more: [src/arbiter/supply_deps.py](../../src/arbiter/supply_deps.py) docstring)
- [tooling.py](../../src/arbiter/tooling.py): Plan and verify the external tools Arbiter can use. 12 public functions.
- [verify.py](../../src/arbiter/verify.py): The model verification pass: a second opinion on each finding, never a filter. Defines `Reply`, `VerifyProvider`, `Excerpt`. 17 public functions. Why: The verdict is recorded on the finding as `verification`. Nothing is hidden, deleted or re-graded here: the tier mapping (Phase 1) reads the verdict and decides whether a finding may block a gate. (more: [src/arbiter/verify.py](../../src/arbiter/verify.py) docstring)

## Package tools

- [ai_corpus_generate.py](../../tools/ai_corpus_generate.py): Generate the AI-written-code corpus with a separate model run. Defines `Budget`. 6 public functions. Why: Each app is one headless Claude Code run (`claude -p`) in an empty directory, given a neutral "build this" prompt: no mention of security, error handling, review or the defects the corpus is meant to measure. (more: [tools/ai_corpus_generate.py](../../tools/ai_corpus_generate.py) docstring)
- [ai_corpus_score.py](../../tools/ai_corpus_score.py): Score Arbiter on AI-written apps against hand labels: recall, precision, misses. Defines `AppScore`. 19 public functions. Why: The corpus is fixtures/ai-corpus/<lang>/<task>/: `app/` is what a model wrote when asked to build the task (see manifest.json for the prompt, model and date), and `labels.json` beside it is the defects a reviewer found by reading `app/`. (more: [tools/ai_corpus_score.py](../../tools/ai_corpus_score.py) docstring)
- [bootstrap_repo.sh](../../tools/bootstrap_repo.sh): _No module docstring._ 3 public functions.
- [calibrate_external.py](../../tools/calibrate_external.py): Assign severities to a third-party tool's checks by measuring them. 3 public functions. Why: Checkov's open build reports `"severity": null` on every finding. So does bandit's per-test confidence in practice, and gitleaks has no notion of severity at all. (more: [tools/calibrate_external.py](../../tools/calibrate_external.py) docstring)
- [corpus.py](../../tools/corpus.py): Run Arbiter across a corpus of repositories and summarize signal vs noise. 2 public functions.
- [disagree.py](../../tools/disagree.py): Find the findings where the tools disagree, and send those to be judged. 3 public functions. Why: The informative ones are the findings where two independent analyzers looked at the same line and reached different conclusions. (more: [tools/disagree.py](../../tools/disagree.py) docstring)
- [discriminate.py](../../tools/discriminate.py): Measure whether each rule actually tells good code apart from bad code. 2 public functions. Why: A rule is worth its severity only if it fires more on code that is broken than on code that is not. Everything else -- how serious the underlying idea sounds, how many findings it produces, how confident the regex is -- is beside the point. (more: [tools/discriminate.py](../../tools/discriminate.py) docstring)
- [fetch_corpus.sh](../../tools/fetch_corpus.sh): _No module docstring._ 4 public functions.
- [fetch_heldout_r5.sh](../../tools/fetch_heldout_r5.sh): _No module docstring._ 1 public function.
- [fixpairs.py](../../tools/fixpairs.py): Mine real before/after pairs from repository history. 4 public functions. Why: Everything else Arbiter measures against, it made. (more: [tools/fixpairs.py](../../tools/fixpairs.py) docstring)
- [gold_benchmark.py](../../tools/gold_benchmark.py): Gold-standard benchmark: how often each rule fires on exemplary code (ARB-065). Defines `Pin`. 22 public functions. Why: Precision mode scans every gold repository named in `tools/fetch_corpus.sh` (the `get_pinned` lines: name, url, sha, language) and counts findings per rule, per repository and per thousand lines of code. (more: [tools/gold_benchmark.py](../../tools/gold_benchmark.py) docstring)
- [inject.py](../../tools/inject.py): Defect injection: measured recall and specificity at scale. Defines `Seeds`, `Case`. 55 public functions. Why: Seeds come from the public corpus rather than from templates, because effective sample size is bounded by generator diversity, not by trial count. (more: [tools/inject.py](../../tools/inject.py) docstring)
- [install_tools.sh](../../tools/install_tools.sh): _No module docstring._ 7 public functions.
- [integrity.py](../../tools/integrity.py): Claim-integrity evidence harness. 9 public functions. Why: Verdict correctness on arbitrary code is undecidable. Claim integrity is a property of Arbiter's own execution, so it can be enumerated.
- [label_models.py](../../tools/label_models.py): Independent model labels for Arbiter findings: two labellers, one adjudicator (ARB-067). Defines `Budget`, `Cache`, `Labeller`. 31 public functions. Why: Nothing here runs the code it reads, and code leaves the machine only as the bounded excerpt in the prompt.
- [label_populations.py](../../tools/label_populations.py): Backfill the population fields of existing label files, with no model calls. 10 public functions. Why: Only the population fields (`label_sample.POPULATION_KEYS`, plus `population_from`) are written; a record whose other fields would change is refused, so no verdict, labeller or split can move. (more: [tools/label_populations.py](../../tools/label_populations.py) docstring)
- [label_sample.py](../../tools/label_sample.py): Human labelling for measured precision: sample findings, then score the labels. 15 public functions. Why: The gold benchmark's per-KLOC budgets assume every finding on exemplary code is a false positive. That is an assumption, not a measurement: some of those findings are true. This turns it into a measurement. (more: [tools/label_sample.py](../../tools/label_sample.py) docstring)
- [mutate_tests.py](../../tools/mutate_tests.py): Put each defect back and check the test that should catch it does. Defines `Mutation`. 2 public functions. Why: A test suite that has never failed is not evidence. (more: [tools/mutate_tests.py](../../tools/mutate_tests.py) docstring)
- [planted_score.py](../../tools/planted_score.py): Score the planted corpus per language: what is caught, missed, or misfired. 1 public function. Why: The corpus and its markers are described in src/arbiter/planted.py.
- [precision_guard.py](../../tools/precision_guard.py): CI precision guard: a rule may be gate-eligible only on evidence. 5 public functions. Why: The sibling of tools/regression_guard.py: that one asks whether findings changed, this one whether the precision claim still rests on its labels.
- [precision_ledger.py](../../tools/precision_ledger.py): Build the per-rule precision ledger from label files. 23 public functions. Why: The ledger is rebuilt from the label files every time, never edited by hand: the label files are the evidence and the ledger is arithmetic on them. (more: [tools/precision_ledger.py](../../tools/precision_ledger.py) docstring)
- [regression_guard.py](../../tools/regression_guard.py): Regression guards: saved finding snapshots and scan-time budgets. Defines `Target`, `Result`. 25 public functions. Why: Targets are listed in tools/gold/guards.json; snapshots and the time baseline live in tools/gold/snapshots/. (more: [tools/regression_guard.py](../../tools/regression_guard.py) docstring)
- [rule_requirements.py](../../tools/rule_requirements.py): Propose `requirements: [ARB-xxx]` for every shipped rule, from evidence. 12 public functions.
- [train_cycle.sh](../../tools/train_cycle.sh): _No module docstring._
- [variants.py](../../tools/variants.py): Mutation variants: does a rule still fire when the defect is written differently? Defines `Rewrite`. 18 public functions. Why: The planted corpus (fixtures/planted/<lang>/bad) states each defect once, in the shape its author thought of. (more: [tools/variants.py](../../tools/variants.py) docstring)
- [worklist.py](../../tools/worklist.py): Turn a training cycle's measurements into a ranked list of things to fix. 1 public function. Why: A training cycle produces a lot of numbers and no instructions. Somebody -- a person, or a Claude session opening this repository weeks from now with no memory of the last one -- then has to read all of it and work out what to do. (more: [tools/worklist.py](../../tools/worklist.py) docstring)

## Package tools/ground_truth

- [benchmarks_gt.py](../../tools/ground_truth/benchmarks_gt.py): Ground-truth labels from benchmarks with published answers (ARB-067). 5 public functions. Why: A finding whose CWE the case says nothing about gets no label here: the benchmark answers one question per case. Findings outside the case files (the benchmarks' harness code) are ignored.
- [cve_pairs.py](../../tools/ground_truth/cve_pairs.py): CVE fix pairs: scan the vulnerable and the fixed version, label what moved (ARB-067). 5 public functions. Why: Suspects are not labelled here; `label_models.py` labels them. Only the fix's own files are scanned, so project-level rules (manifests, docs) never see a whole project and are left out of the suspects.
- [cve_select.py](../../tools/ground_truth/cve_select.py): Pick CVE fix pairs from GitHub Security Advisories and pin them (ARB-067). 5 public functions. Why: For each language's ecosystem (pip, npm, go, maven, rubygems) and each CWE Arbiter claims, this walks reviewed advisories newest first and keeps one whose references include a GitHub fix commit that
- [external_scorecard.py](../../tools/ground_truth/external_scorecard.py): External conformance scorecard: Arbiter against benchmarks it did not write (ARB-120). Defines `Unit`, `Stratum`, `Scored`. 25 public functions. Why: Every number is a benchmark-conformance figure scoped to that benchmark and its label method, never a 99% or production-population claim. Output is aggregate-only: no case names, file paths, advisory IDs or excerpts. (more: [tools/ground_truth/external_scorecard.py](../../tools/ground_truth/external_scorecard.py) docstring)
- [fetch_gt.sh](../../tools/ground_truth/fetch_gt.sh): _No module docstring._ 1 public function.
- [ghsa_pairs.py](../../tools/ground_truth/ghsa_pairs.py): Fetch, scan and score the frozen GHSA fix pairs (ARB-121). 13 public functions. Why: Development pairs are reported in detail. Sealed pairs are scanned in memory and only per-language and overall aggregates are written: no per-pair row, CWE cell, finding or excerpt of a sealed pair reaches disk.
- [ghsa_select.py](../../tools/ground_truth/ghsa_select.py): Select and freeze real-CVE fix pairs from the GitHub Advisory Database (ARB-121). Defines `RateLimited`, `Cache`. 18 public functions. Why: An external benchmark for the five supported languages: reviewed GitHub Security Advisories (advisory data CC-BY-4.0) whose fix is a GitHub commit touching source in that language, restricted to the CWEs a native security rule of that language's pack is tagged with, so that recall is measured on weaknesses Arbiter claims to look for. (more: [tools/ground_truth/ghsa_select.py](../../tools/ground_truth/ghsa_select.py) docstring)
- [gt_common.py](../../tools/ground_truth/gt_common.py): Shared pieces of the ground-truth and model-labelling tools (ARB-067). 16 public functions. Why: Nothing here runs the code it reads.
- [heldout_split.py](../../tools/ground_truth/heldout_split.py): Freeze the held-out split the precision claim is reported on (ARB-067). 3 public functions. Why: The file is written once and then frozen: rerunning with the same seed and pins gives the same split, and `--check` fails if the committed file and a fresh computation disagree. (more: [tools/ground_truth/heldout_split.py](../../tools/ground_truth/heldout_split.py) docstring)
- [realvuln_conformance.py](../../tools/ground_truth/realvuln_conformance.py): Aggregate-only case-level conformance scoring for the approved RealVuln slice. Defines `EvaluationError`. 3 public functions.

## Package tools/panel

- [panel.py](../../tools/panel/panel.py): An independent labelling panel of models from different companies (ARB-122). Defines `Seat`, `Panel`. 9 public functions. Why: Independence is enforced, not assumed: two seats that resolve to one vendor are refused (the later seat is dropped and the run says so), Copilot never seats an Anthropic model, and an answer from a model other than the one its seat resolved to is discarded. (more: [tools/panel/panel.py](../../tools/panel/panel.py) docstring)
- [providers.py](../../tools/panel/providers.py): Model providers for the labelling panel (ARB-122): one interface over the Claude, Codex, Gemini and Copilot command-line tools, each on the user's own subscription (no API keys), plus a fake for tests. Defines `ProviderError`, `UsageLimit`, `Unavailable`, `ParseError` (+7 more). 4 public functions. Why: Vendor independence is the panel's whole value, so each answer carries the model that produced it and `model_vendor` maps it to the company that made it. The panel refuses two seats of one vendor (tools/panel/panel.py).
